title: OECS Hardware Definitions
description: Defines the physical/hardware specification of an EV charger: housing, electrical input/output, protection, connectors, user interface, connectivity, and safety systems.

formFactor.description: Physical mounting/enclosure style. 'freestanding' covers self-contained units that stand on their own base on the ground (posts, columns, larger cabinets); 'cabinet' is for a separate power-electronics enclosure in split systems, paired with a smaller wall- or freestanding-mounted user-facing dispenser.

electricalInput.description: Characteristics of the grid/supply connection feeding the charger.

maxCurrent.description: Maximum input current draw, unit typically 'A'.

connectionType.description: Whether the unit is permanently hardwired to the supply or connects via an industrial plug.

efficiency.description: Rated AC-to-DC (or pass-through) conversion efficiency in percent, at rated load.

powerOutput.description: Aggregate power delivery capability of the charger (a single connector's individual rating is described in the connector object).

ratedOutputVoltage.description: Unit typically 'V'. Relevant primarily for DC chargers.

simultaneousChargingSupported.description: Only meaningful when there are 2+ connectors. True if more than one connector can actively deliver power at once; false if a second connector just queues behind the first (only one session runs at a time even though multiple connectors exist).

dynamicPowerSharing.description: Only meaningful when there are 2+ connectors. Whether the charger dynamically splits/reallocates its total power budget across concurrently active sessions, rather than each connector having a fixed independent rating.

protection.description: Electrical protection and safety devices built into the charger.

types.description: RCD/RCM types integrated, per IEC 62955 / IEC 60755 classification.

external.description: True if RCD protection must be supplied externally (upstream) rather than being integrated.

surgeProtection.description: SPD class per IEC 61643, e.g. 'Type 1', 'Type 2', 'Type 1+2'. Omit if the charger has no surge protection device.

features.description: Protection features present, beyond RCD/surge/overvoltage handled by the more detailed fields above. 'insulation-monitoring' (IMD) is typically required on DC chargers.

electrical.description: The charger's electrical characteristics: grid supply (input), delivery capability (output), and protection devices, grouped together since all three describe the same electrical system.

languageSupport.description: BCP 47 language tags supported by the on-device UI.

connectivity.description: Physical/network connectivity hardware, distinct from the application-layer protocols described in the software specification.

interfaces.description: Physical interfaces present besides Wi-Fi/cellular, which are detailed separately below. 'powerline-communication' is PLC per ISO 15118 / IEC 61851, used for HLC over the charging cable's CP/PP lines.

wifi.description: Supported Wi-Fi standards. Omit the field (or leave empty) if the charger has no Wi-Fi radio.

cellular.description: Omit this field entirely if the charger has no cellular radio.

meter.description: The charger's primary energy meter, used for session metering and (where billing-grade) invoicing.

integrated.description: True if the meter is built into the charger; false if metering is provided by a separate, externally installed meter.

certification.description: Legal metrology certification, e.g. 'MID (2014/32/EU)', 'ANSI C12.20', 'Eichrecht'. Its presence is what makes metering suitable for direct billing/invoicing; omit if the meter has no such certification.

hardware.description: Complete hardware specification of the charger.

certifications.description: Formal certifications tied to the hardware/enclosure as a whole (e.g. safety, EMC, type approval). Certifications specific to a single protocol belong on that protocol entry instead (software.protocols[].certifications); certifications that don't fit either place (e.g. company-wide quality management) belong in metadata.certificates.
